name: M3E Canvas
tagline: A browser sketchpad for app screens that turns your drawing into a prompt (written instructions) an AI coding tool can build from.
sentence: Drag real app parts (buttons, cards, menus) onto phone screens in your browser, connect the screens, and press Export: it writes a plain-English brief you paste into Claude Code or another AI coding tool to build the real app.

visual.alt: M3E Canvas's own screenshot: two connected phone screens for a notes app (a home list called 'メモ' and a meeting-detail screen) sketched on the canvas, with the right-hand panel showing the exported prompt written out in Japanese - it names the app, describes it as a simple notes app opened from a list to edit, lists the Material 3 purple color theme by hex code (primary #6750A4 and more), and ends in a 'Copy prompt' button.
visual.caption: From the README's own docs folder: sketch the screens on the left, get the finished prompt on the right. This demo happens to be in Japanese, one of the four languages it can write in.

board.say: You can tell an AI coding tool what app screen you want in plain words, but words alone get the layout wrong.
board.eg: "Make me an app with a bottom nav and a card list" comes out differently every time you ask - you end up fixing the result instead of describing it better.

board.say: You open the free web app and start dragging parts onto a screen - no sign-up, nothing to install.
board.eg: It runs at lnkiai.github.io/m3e-canvas - open it in Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge and you're sketching.

board.say: The screens you want, and which button leads to which screen.
board.eg: Buttons, cards, list items, navigation bars, search bars and dozens of other Material 3 Expressive parts, arranged across as many screens as you like.

board.say: It watches how you arrange the parts and connect the screens, then turns that into words.
steps: You drag parts onto the canvas and arrange them the way you want the screen to look
You give buttons a target screen (or "back") and pick a look: color theme, corner shape, type and motion style
The Tidy button auto-aligns everything - bars to the edges, buttons and list items joined up - so a sloppy layout doesn't turn into a sloppy prompt
You press Export and it writes the whole thing out as a plain-language brief, including what each part does, not just what it looks like
board.eg: The README's own demo: sketch a recipes app, change its color theme, copy the prompt, hand it to an AI coding tool, and run the result on Android.

board.say: A brief you can hand straight to an AI coding tool.

outputs.what: A ready-to-paste prompt in your choice of language
outputs.eg: English, Japanese, Chinese or Korean - describing every screen, color and behavior
Save any screen as a PNG file

outputs.what: A link that hands your design straight to an AI coding agent
outputs.eg: The beta "AI draft" link has an agent read the sketch and reply with a link to what it built

before: Describing a screen in plain words to an AI coding tool gets the layout wrong more often than it gets it right.
Figma and other design tools export pictures or files aimed at human developers - nothing an AI coding tool can read as instructions.
Material 3 Expressive is new enough that most AI coding tools don't know its specific shapes and rules unless you spell them out.
after: Sketch it instead of describing it, and the tool writes the words for you - including what each part should do, not just what it looks like.
The output is one plain-text prompt any AI coding tool accepts: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more.
It's free and open source, and runs entirely in your browser - nothing to install, and your sketches never leave your own computer.
uses_note: It's 25 days old, and the coverage so far describes what it does rather than a documented story of someone using it to ship something specific - real use is still early.

steps: [Open the live app](https://lnkiai.github.io/m3e-canvas/) in your browser - free, no sign-up, nothing to install.
Drag a few parts onto the canvas (a button, a card, a nav bar) and connect them with tap-through navigation.
Click Export, pick English, copy the prompt, and paste it into Claude Code (or any AI coding tool) and ask it to build the app.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/lnkiai/m3e-canvas

If that scan passes: open the live app, sketch a two-screen mock (a list screen and a detail screen), connect them with tap-through navigation, export the prompt, and show me exactly what the exported text says. 10 minutes max, then stop and report back in plain English.

best_for: You want to hand an AI coding tool a real design instead of a paragraph, and you don't have Figma skills
You're prototyping an Android or web screen and want Material 3 Expressive done right without learning its rules by hand
skip_if: You need a different design system - Fluent, Carbon, Ant Design or your own - this only knows Material 3 Expressive
You need your sketches backed up or shared with a team - everything lives only in your own browser's storage, with no cloud sync yet

alternatives.name: Google Stitch
alternatives.line: Google's AI tool that generates app and web screens from a written description, instead of you arranging the parts by hand.

alternatives.name: Figma
alternatives.line: The design app most product teams use: you draw every screen yourself, with far more control and far more to learn.

watch: **Only Material 3 Expressive.** A different design system - Fluent, Carbon, your own brand system - isn't supported at all.
**No cloud save yet.** Everything lives in your browser's local storage; clear your browser data and your sketches are gone. There's no export-to-file backup.

**The optional AI helper sends your design to whichever provider you pick.** Turn on the AI tab and your design description goes from your browser straight to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or DeepSeek using your own key. Normal use - dragging parts, exporting a prompt - sends nothing anywhere.
**25 days old, with a small team.** 10 contributors so far and fast-moving weekly changes - expect rough edges and quick changes to how things look.

footprint.disk: Zero to use the [hosted app](https://lnkiai.github.io/m3e-canvas/) - it opens straight in your browser and nothing downloads to your computer. Running your own local copy needs Node.js and `npm install`; no source states an exact size for that download.
footprint.memory: No data found for an exact number. It's a normal browser tab running a static website, not a separate program on your computer.
footprint.runs_on: Any modern browser - Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge - on Mac, Windows or Linux. No install and no graphics card needed. Running your own copy to develop it further needs Node.js.
